topStories.headline: Voters Pass Prop H in a Landslide, Securing Muni Funding — and the M-Ocean View Line
topStories.dek: San Francisco's parcel-tax measure for Muni passed with roughly 73% of the vote on Tuesday, pulling the agency back from the edge of deep service cuts that would have hit M-line riders hardest.
topStories.body:
San Francisco voters gave Muni an overwhelming financial lifeline on Election Day, November 3, approving Proposition H by roughly 73% to 27% in preliminary results. The measure — which still requires certification by the Department of Elections on December 3 — creates an annual parcel tax expected to generate approximately $177 million a year for Muni operations over the next 15 years.

For residents of West Portal, Stonestown, and Lakeshore who depend on the M-Ocean View line, the stakes were unusually direct. The SFMTA had warned that without new revenue it would be forced to eliminate up to 20 Muni routes and double wait times on Metro lines, potentially ending or severely curtailing M-line service through the Twin Peaks Tunnel.

Most single-family homeowners in the neighborhoods will see an annual increase of about $129 on their property tax bills, with multifamily parcels starting at $249 and commercial properties at $799. A companion regional measure, RTM, which would raise sales taxes across five Bay Area counties to shore up BART and other regional transit, also carried San Francisco with more than 78% support.

The double victory surprised some transit advocates who had feared voter fatigue with tax measures. Backers framed both measures as essential for a transit system they called a lifeline for workers, seniors, and students throughout the city's west side.

topStories.headline: SFSU Braces for Possible Faculty Strike as Union Vote Runs Through November 19
topStories.dek: The California Faculty Association is in the middle of a strike-authorization vote that could shut down San Francisco State — and 22 other CSU campuses — before the semester ends.
topStories.body:
A strike-authorization vote that could upend the fall semester at San Francisco State University is under way, with ballots open from October 26 through November 19. The California Faculty Association, which represents roughly 29,000 professors, lecturers, librarians, and counselors across the California State University system, launched the vote after declaring a bargaining impasse in July following 16 months of stalled negotiations.

At SFSU's campus in Lakeshore, faculty and students have already rallied publicly. On October 29, union members from multiple campus unions marched to the administration building and announced they were preparing to shut down the university if a strike were called. Students who joined the action said the quality of their own education is directly linked to the conditions their instructors work under.

The CFA's main demands include meaningful salary increases — faculty have gone without a raise since 2024 and the union's contract expired at the end of last year — along with caps on class sizes, stronger job security for lecturers, and explicit protections governing the university's use of artificial intelligence in instruction. The CSU system has reached tentative agreements with three smaller unions covering about 14,000 employees, but those deals have not resolved the core dispute with the faculty union.

If a majority of voting members authorize a strike, CFA leadership will have the power to call a work stoppage at any point. No date has been set, and talks could resume before the vote closes. Students are advised to monitor SFSU communications for any changes to their class schedules.

topStories.headline: Sbarro Is Coming Back to Stonestown — and Blondie's Pizza Is Out After an Eviction Fight
topStories.dek: The national chain will return to Stonestown Galleria's food court in early 2027, four years after Blondie's Pizza took its spot, following a dispute over more than $74,000 in unpaid rent.
topStories.body:
Stonestown Galleria confirmed this week that Sbarro will return to the mall's food court in the first quarter of 2027, ending a four-year absence that began when local chain Blondie's Pizza moved in after the national brand departed. The swap is coming by way of a legal dispute: the mall's operator sued Blondie's earlier this year, alleging the restaurant owed more than $74,000 in unpaid rent. The SF Standard reported the mall had issued a default notice and later a pay-or-vacate order before the closure was finalized.

The announcement quickly stirred a wave of nostalgia on social media among shoppers who remembered Sbarro as a staple of the Stonestown food court experience. The mall has continued adding tenants even as downtown San Francisco's retail sector has struggled, and the return of a recognizable brand fits a broader pattern of Stonestown extending its reach as a neighborhood commercial anchor on the city's west side.

Stonestown's redevelopment plan — approved by the Planning Commission in 2024 and envisions transforming the surface parking lots into thousands of new homes and additional retail space — continues to move through the pipeline, though no construction start date for the residential towers has been announced.

events.title: Great Dickens Christmas Fair — 42nd Season

Tickets from $35; active-duty military admitted free the first two weekends.

events.title: SF International Hip Hop DanceFest

moreNews.headline: SFSU to Launch 'Study Abroad @ San Francisco' Program in Spring 2027
moreNews.body: San Francisco State University announced in October 2026 that it will launch a new program called Study Abroad @ San Francisco beginning in Spring 2027. The program is designed to bring international students to the Lakeshore campus for immersive study, adding a new international enrollment stream as the university navigates ongoing budget pressures.
moreNews.sourceName: SFSU College of Professional & Global Education

moreNews.headline: SFSU Closed Wednesday, November 11 for Veterans Day
moreNews.body: San Francisco State University will be closed on Wednesday, November 11, in observance of Veterans Day. All classes and administrative offices will be shut for the holiday; students should check their course pages for any instructor-specific guidance about assignments due around the holiday.
moreNews.sourceName: SFSU College of Professional & Global Education
